thesis: Profitable oncology company with 1.40B cash and marketable securities, no borrowings, TTM free cash flow about 1.16B and shrinking share count (244.0M vs 278.5M weighted diluted in Q3 2025). Cabometyx patent litigation protects the main product at least until a January 2030 earliest approval date for MSN's generic, with settlements at January 2031, which gives about four years of cash flow; zanzalintinib (NDA PDUFA 2027-03-03) is the pipeline option.
counterthesis: About 92 percent of Q3 revenue is one drug (Cabometyx 603.2M of 658.7M total) with a defined loss of exclusivity 2030 to 2031; a November 2026 trial on the separate '039 patent could shorten that. The FDA extended zanzalintinib review by three months after a major amendment. TTM operating cash flow (1.17B) was helped by a one time federal cash tax benefit from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, so free cash flow overstates the run rate. Buybacks at an average 54.03 compare with the single source close of 68.71, so recent repurchases are less accretive.
invalidation: Adverse ruling in the November 2026 '039 patent trial moving generic entry earlier; Cabometyx quarterly sales falling year over year; zanzalintinib complete response or negative STELLAR-304 topline (expected Q1 2027); cash returned via buybacks outrunning free cash flow.
